title: Earth Observation for Disaster Mapping: Benchmarks, Methods, Challenges and Future Perspectives
affiliations: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology
abstractSummary: The paper reviews and benchmarks Earth-observation methods for disaster mapping. It separates disaster extent mapping from infrastructure damage mapping, compares traditional methods, deep learning models, and foundation models, and studies reproducibility across a standardized benchmark suite.

reportedFindings: Architectural complexity has diminishing returns for disaster extent mapping.
Change-detection architectures are more useful for infrastructure damage mapping than for extent mapping.
Foundation models do not consistently outperform task-specific baselines, especially on non-RGB modalities.

codeRepository.name: AnyDisasterMapping
codeRepository.description: Official code repository for the EO-based disaster mapping review and benchmark.
installation: Install PyTorch, torchvision, and xformers with a CUDA-compatible wheel index.
Install the repository in editable mode with pip.
Build optional ChangeMamba selective scan kernels when using ChangeMamba.
Place pretrained checkpoints under pretrained_weight/ for supported model families.

layout.src/core: Trainer, config loader, registry, augmentation, and metrics.
layout.src/tasks: Task handlers for segmentation, change detection, and semantic change detection.
layout.src/datasets: Dataset adapters and runtime data contracts.
layout.src/models: Model wrappers and vendored third-party implementations.
layout.configs: Experiment configurations grouped by disaster domain and dataset.
layout.scripts/data_prep: Dataset preparation guides and helper scripts.

sourceNotes: Paper metadata and DOI were verified from SSRN search metadata and the official GitHub README.
Repository content was summarized from the official GitHub README instead of mirroring the full paper text.
